tools.name: list_tag_providers
tools.title: List tag providers
tools.description: Lists the tag providers configured on this gateway.

tools.name: browse_tags
tools.title: Browse tags
tools.description: Browses the tag tree. Start at the root with an empty path, then drill in. Set recursive=true to walk folders, bounded by maxDepth and limit.

path.description: Tag path to browse, e.g. '[default]Area1/Line2'. Empty browses the provider root.

provider.description: Tag provider name. Ignored when 'path' includes [provider]. Defaults to 'default'.

recursive.description: Recurse into folders and UDT instances.

limit.description: Maximum number of nodes to return.

tools.name: read_tags
tools.title: Read tag values
tools.description: Reads current values for one or more tag paths, with quality and timestamp.

tools.name: get_tag_config
tools.title: Get tag configuration
tools.description: Returns the full JSON configuration of tags or folders — data type, bindings, alarms, history settings and UDT parameters. Use this to understand how a tag is built, not just its current value.

paths.description: Tag or folder paths to fetch configuration for.

recursive.description: Include the configuration of child tags.

localOnly.description: Exclude configuration inherited from a UDT definition.

tools.name: write_tags
tools.title: Write tag values
tools.description: Writes values to tags. This changes live process values — confirm the paths with read_tags first.

value.description: Value to write (string, number, boolean or null).

tools.name: configure_tags
tools.title: Create or edit tag configuration
tools.description:
Creates or edits tags, UDT definitions and UDT instances. Each entry in 'tags' is a configuration object in the same shape get_tag_config returns, carrying its own 'name'; 'parentPath' is the folder they go into. Write UDT definitions to the provider's _types_ folder, e.g. parentPath '[default]_types_'.

Collisions default to MergeOverwrite: properties you send are applied and properties you leave out keep their current values, so editing one setting does not require sending the whole tag. Use Overwrite only when you mean to REPLACE the configuration — it drops every property you did not send, including alarms and history settings. Use Abort to refuse to touch anything that already exists.

The configuration is validated first and the whole call is refused if anything is wrong, because Ignition's own parser accepts several broken inputs silently — most notably a UDT parameter given a value but no dataType, which it discards while reporting success.

Validation is not the only way a tag can fail. The provider can still refuse an individual one — an Abort collision being the ordinary case — so compare 'written' against 'attempted', or read 'ok' per entry in 'results'. A refusal leaves that tag exactly as it was.

parentPath.description: Folder the tags are created in, e.g. '[default]Area1', '[default]' for the provider root, or '[default]_types_' for UDT definitions.

tags.description: Tag configuration objects, each with its own 'name'.

collisionPolicy.description: What to do when a tag already exists at that path.

tools.name: delete_tags
tools.title: Delete tags
tools.description: Removes tags, folders or UDT definitions and everything under them. Deleting a UDT definition breaks every instance of it, so check with browse_tags first. This cannot be undone from here.

tools.name: rename_tag
tools.title: Rename a tag
tools.description: Renames a tag in place. This is a real rename rather than a delete and recreate, so tag history and UDT instance membership survive it — but every reference to the old path, in bindings, scripts and other tags, breaks.

newName.description: The new name. Not a path — the tag stays where it is.

tools.name: import_tags
tools.title: Import a tag export
tools.description:
Applies a whole Designer-style tag export in one call. Use it to move a folder or a type library; for individual tags configure_tags is easier to get right, since it validates each one and reports per-tag results.

Pass exactly what system.tag.exportTags produced, unchanged, and do NOT reshape it into configure_tags' 'tags' array — the two tools take deliberately different shapes. Note the export shape depends on how many paths were exported: one path yields a bare object, several yield an object wrapping a 'tags' array. This tool accepts both, which is exactly why passing it through untouched is the rule.

Check 'imported' against 'total' rather than 'findings'. A malformed payload fails in Ignition's parser rather than in validation, so it surfaces in 'qualities' and leaves 'findings' empty — a response that looks clean apart from imported being 0. Nothing is partially written when that happens.

parentPath.description: Folder to import into, e.g. '[default]Area1' or '[default]' for the root.

json.description: The tag export JSON, as a string, exactly as system.tag.exportTags emitted it.

collisionPolicy.description: What to do where the export overlaps existing tags.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: Lists the projects on this gateway with their inheritance and enabled state.

tools.name: list_project_resources
tools.title: List project resources
tools.description: Lists resources in a project. Filter by module id and/or resource type to narrow it down — for example moduleId 'com.inductiveautomation.perspective' with type 'views' lists Perspective views, and moduleId 'ignition' type 'script-python' lists project script modules. Call with no filter first to discover what types exist.

project.description: Project name.

moduleId.description: Only return resources owned by this module id.

type.description: Only return resources of this resource type.

pathContains.description: Only return resources whose path contains this substring (case-insensitive).

limit.description: Maximum number of resources to return.

tools.name: read_project_resource
tools.title: Read a project resource
tools.description: Returns the contents of one project resource. Perspective views come back as view.json, Python scripts as code.py. Use list_project_resources to find the exact moduleId, type and path.

project.description: Project name.

moduleId.description: Module id that owns the resource.

path.description: Resource path within the type, e.g. 'Page/Main'.

dataKey.description: Which data file to read. Defaults to the resource's single/primary file.

maxBytes.description: Truncate the returned content beyond this many bytes.

tools.name: scan_resource_files
tools.title: Scan resource files from disk
tools.description: Makes the gateway re-read its resources from disk and load what is actually there. Use it after files were edited directly, or after a git checkout, pull, branch switch or stash, so the running gateway matches the working tree. On Ignition 8.3 this is the ONLY thing that makes a disk edit take effect: 8.3 never scans on its own. Two collections: 'projects' is data/projects (views, scripts, named queries) and 'config' is data/config (tags, device connections, themes) which exists only on 8.3. This scans EVERY project, not one — a project directory that has appeared is registered, and a project whose directory is GONE is deleted from the gateway, so check with the user before running it against a working tree you don't recognise. Follow up with read_project_resource to confirm the new contents actually loaded.

target.description: Which collection to scan. 'config' is Ignition 8.3 only.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the scan to finish. The scan carries on regardless — only the wait is bounded.

tools.name: list_datasources
tools.title: List database connections
tools.description: Lists the gateway's database connections and their current status.

tools.name: run_query
tools.title: Run a SQL query
tools.description: Runs a SELECT against a gateway database connection and returns the rows. Use parameters rather than string-concatenating values. Row count is capped by 'limit'. This tool refuses anything that isn't a SELECT or WITH — use it for analysis, not for changing data.

sql.description: SQL to run. Use '?' placeholders for parameters.

params.description: Values for the '?' placeholders, in order.

tools.name: query_tag_history
tools.title: Query tag history
tools.description: Queries the historian for one or more tags over a time window. Give either 'rangeMinutes' (relative to now) or explicit ISO-8601 'startDate'/'endDate'.

rangeMinutes.description: Look back this many minutes from now.

endDate.description: ISO-8601 end. Defaults to now when startDate is given.

aggregation.description: Aggregation mode applied to each interval.

returnSize.description: Number of intervals to return. Use 0 for raw on-change values.

tools.name: gateway_info
tools.title: Gateway info
tools.description: Overall gateway status: version, edition, redundancy role, running state and licensed tag usage. Start here when diagnosing a gateway you don't know.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.title: List modules
tools.description: Lists installed gateway modules with version and running state, including any fault reason for modules that failed to start.

tools.name: query_logs
tools.title: Query gateway logs
tools.description: Searches the gateway's log. This is usually the fastest way to find out why something is failing. Narrow with minLevel and searchTerms rather than pulling everything.

loggers.description: Only include these logger names (exact match).

searchTerms.description: Only include events whose message contains these terms.

rangeMinutes.description: Look back this many minutes from now.

tools.name: list_active_alarms
tools.title: List active alarms
tools.description: Returns the gateway's current alarm status — what is active and what is unacknowledged right now.

tools.name: run_script
tools.title: Run a Jython script (gateway scope)
tools.description: Executes Python (Jython) in gateway scope with the project's script context, giving access to the whole system.* API. This is arbitrary code execution on the gateway — prefer a purpose-built tool when one exists, and read the script back to the user before running it. Assign to a variable named 'result' to return a value.

project.description: Project whose script context to run in. Defaults to the first project.

tools.name: reset_trial
tools.title: Reset the gateway trial timer
tools.description: Restarts the gateway's two-hour trial countdown — the same action as the 'Reset Trial' button on the gateway home page. By default this only works once the trial has actually expired, which is the rule Ignition itself enforces; pass force=true to top the timer up mid-session. Refused on an activated gateway, where there is no trial to reset. Use this when gateway_info shows demoTimeRemaining at 0 and tags, history or Perspective have stopped working.

force.description: Reset even if the trial hasn't expired yet, topping the timer back up to two hours.

tools.name: thread_dump
tools.title: Dump gateway threads
tools.description: Every thread in the gateway JVM: a state histogram, a per-subsystem breakdown grouped by thread name (Ignition names threads like 'perspective-worker-3', so the groups read as subsystems), any deadlock, and stack traces for the threads using the most CPU. Cumulative CPU here is measured since gateway startup — use thread_hotspots to see what is busy right now.

nameContains.description: Only include threads whose name contains this substring.

topN.description: How many threads to report in full, ranked by cumulative CPU time.

includeStacks.description: Include stack traces for the reported threads.

maxFrames.description: Truncate each stack trace to this many frames.

tools.name: thread_hotspots
tools.title: Sample thread CPU usage
tools.description: Samples per-thread CPU time twice over a short window and ranks threads by how much they burned in between, with the stack each was running at the end. This is the tool for 'what is pegging this gateway right now'. Note it blocks for the sample window before returning.

sampleSeconds.description: Length of the sampling window, 1-30 seconds.

topN.description: How many threads to report, ranked by CPU used during the window.

maxFrames.description: Truncate each stack trace to this many frames.

tools.name: jvm_health
tools.title: JVM memory, GC and class loading
tools.description: Heap and non-heap usage, per-pool occupancy (which tells you which generation is under pressure), garbage collector counts and times, loaded class counts, direct buffer usage, uptime and the JVM's own launch arguments. Pass sampleSeconds to also measure GC time and process CPU as a percentage of wall clock over a window — a gateway spending a large fraction of its time collecting garbage is slow for a reason no log will show.

sampleSeconds.description: Measure GC and CPU across a window of this many seconds (0-30). 0 reports instantaneous values only and returns immediately.

annotations.title: JVM memory, GC and class loading

tools.name: perspective_list_views
tools.title: List Perspective views
tools.description: Lists the Perspective views in a project, with the number of components in each.

project.description: Project name.

pathContains.description: Only return views whose path contains this substring.

tools.name: perspective_get_view
tools.title: Get a Perspective view
tools.description: Returns a view's parameters, view-level custom properties and its component tree. Each tree entry carries the path you pass to the other perspective_ tools, plus which properties are bound and how many events are attached. Start here before editing.

project.description: Project name.

tools.name: perspective_get_component
tools.title: Get a Perspective component
tools.description: Returns one component in full: type, props, custom properties, bindings (from propConfig), events, position and the names of its children.

project.description: Project name.

tools.name: perspective_list_component_types
tools.title: List Perspective component types
tools.description: Lists the component types registered on this system, which is what perspective_add_component will accept. Filter by category or a substring of the id.

category.description: Only return components in this palette category.

idContains.description: Only return components whose id contains this substring.

tools.name: perspective_get_component_type
tools.title: Get a Perspective component type
tools.description: Returns a component type's default properties, events and extension functions. 'defaultProperties' is the shape a new instance starts with and is the best reference for what the component accepts; perspective_validate_view then enforces the component's real JSON schema.

tools.name: perspective_validate_view
tools.title: Validate a Perspective view
tools.description: Checks a view against the component registry and Perspective's own JSON schemas, and reports the authoring mistakes that break views silently — bindings left in props instead of propConfig, 'bidirectional' at the wrong nesting level, and event scripts missing their leading tab indentation. Each finding says how to fix it.

project.description: Project name.

tools.name: perspective_analyze_performance
tools.title: Analyze Perspective view performance
tools.description: Sweeps a project's views and reports what each costs to open and to keep open — components, bindings, how many of those poll, script transforms, nesting depth and embedded views — alongside findings for the specific things that make a view slow: fast polling, expressions that install their own timers, script transform chains, uncached polled queries, and views repeated many times over by a repeater or carousel. Heaviest views come first. Pass 'view' to analyze a single view instead.

project.description: Project name.

pathContains.description: Only analyze views whose path contains this substring.

limit.description: Maximum number of views to analyze.

minPollSeconds.description: Flag polling bindings faster than this many seconds.

componentBudget.description: Flag views with more components than this.

bindingBudget.description: Flag views with more bindings than this.

depthBudget.description: Flag views nested deeper than this many levels.

tools.name: perspective_list_sessions
tools.title: List Perspective sessions
tools.description: Lists the Perspective sessions currently running on this gateway, with their ids, project, user and open page count. Use an id with perspective_diagnose_live_view.

project.description: Only return sessions for this project.

tools.name: perspective_diagnose_live_view
tools.title: Diagnose a running Perspective view
tools.description: For a view open in a running session, reports every configured property alongside its binding and its CURRENT value and quality. This is how you find out why a binding isn't working: Perspective reports binding failures as bad quality rather than as errors, so a bad quality next to its binding config is usually the whole answer. Only views a user currently has open are visible.

view.description: Only report views whose path contains this substring.

tools.name: perspective_session_performance
tools.title: Perspective session performance
tools.description: What each running session is costing the gateway: queue depth, uptime, page/view/component/binding counts, and timings for the scripts, expressions, fetches and queued tasks it has run. Read queueDepth first — every session serializes all its work through one queue, so a queue that is not draining is a session that feels slow, and it shows there before any average moves. Also reports the gateway-wide script and expression timers. Set includeViews to see which views are mounted and how long each has been resident.

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to report.

includeViews.description: Include the pages and views open in each session, with how long each has been mounted. Component and binding counts are reported per session, not per view.

tools.title: Designer info

tools.title: List resources in the open project

moduleId.description: Only return resources owned by this module id.

type.description: Only return resources of this resource type.

pathContains.description: Only return resources whose path contains this substring (case-insensitive).

limit.description: Maximum number of resources to return.

annotations.title: List resources in the open project

tools.name: read_resource
tools.title: Read a resource from the open project
tools.description: Returns a resource's contents as the Designer sees it, including unsaved edits. Perspective views come back as view.json, scripts as code.py.

moduleId.description: Module id that owns the resource.

dataKey.description: Which data file to read. Defaults to the resource's primary file.

maxBytes.description: Truncate the returned content beyond this many bytes.

annotations.title: Read a resource from the open project

tools.name: list_pending_changes
tools.title: List unsaved Designer changes
tools.description: Lists edits made in this Designer that have not been saved to the gateway yet. Use this to review what write_resource has staged before telling the user to save.

tools.name: merge_gateway_changes
tools.title: Merge gateway changes into this Designer
tools.description: Pulls changes made on the gateway into the open project — the same action as the Designer's 'update available' notification button. Use it after scan_resource_files on the gateway picked up edited files, or when the user says the Designer is showing stale resources. This REFUSES to run when an unsaved Designer edit conflicts with an incoming change, and names the resources, so your edits are never silently overwritten; on a refusal, tell the user to save or discard those resources in the Designer and call this again. Ignition reports no completion for an update, so this watches the project and tells you which resources actually arrived.

waitSeconds.description: How long to watch for merged resources to arrive. The merge carries on regardless — only the wait is bounded.

settleSeconds.description: How long to let a just-finished gateway scan's notification reach this Designer before the conflict check runs. Only paid when there are unsaved edits.

annotations.title: Merge gateway changes into this Designer

tools.name: write_resource
tools.title: Create or update a resource in the open Designer
tools.description: Writes a project resource in the open Designer. The edit is NOT committed — it appears as an unsaved change for the user to review and save, which is the point: keep a human in the loop. Read the resource first so you preserve its existing shape.

moduleId.description: Module id that owns the resource.

dataKey.description: Which data file to write. Defaults to the resource's primary file, or 'data.json' when creating a new resource.

annotations.title: Create or update a resource in the open Designer

tools.name: delete_resource
tools.title: Delete a resource in the open Designer
tools.description: Deletes a project resource in the open Designer. Like write_resource, this is staged as an unsaved change rather than committed.

moduleId.description: Module id that owns the resource.

annotations.title: Delete a resource in the open Designer

tools.name: save_project
tools.title: Save the open project to the gateway
tools.description:
Commits this Designer's staged changes to the gateway — the equivalent of a human pressing Save. Available only because this Designer was started with -Dmcp.designer.allowSave=true.

Refuses when a staged edit conflicts with a change already waiting on the gateway, naming the resources, so a merge is never silently resolved in your favour; run merge_gateway_changes first in that case. Does nothing and reports zero when there is nothing staged. Reports the resource paths it committed, so a script can check rather than assume — list_pending_changes returning 0 afterwards is the invariant.

One limitation worth knowing: this pushes what is in the project tree, and does not flush editors a human has open and unsaved in this Designer. On an unattended Designer there are none. If somebody is working in this one, their open editor's content will not be included.

annotations.title: Save the open project to the gateway

tools.name: perspective_create_view

tools.name: perspective_add_component
tools.title: Add a Perspective component
tools.description: Adds a component to a container. The child position shape comes from the registry — it depends on the PARENT container type, so letting this tool supply it is what makes the component lay out correctly. Properties are NOT pre-filled with the type's defaults: only what you pass in 'props' is written, which is how Perspective stores views and what keeps an absent property meaning 'still at its default'. Call perspective_get_component_type to see what a type accepts. The name is made unique among its siblings automatically.

project.description: Ignored — the Designer operates on the open project.

parentPath.description: Container to add to, e.g. 'root' or 'root/FlexContainer'.

name.description: Component name. Defaults to the type's default, made unique.

props.description: Property values to set. Written as given; defaults are not added.

position.description: Position overrides, merged over the parent's child defaults.

index.description: Insert at this child index. Appends when omitted.
